faq.a: Vedat is associated with the Arabic form وَدَاد, whose core sense is vedat; love, affection (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Vedat?
faq.a: Vedat is associated with Arabic. Vedat is the Turkish form of Arabic وِدَاد (Widād), meaning 'love, affection'.
Yes — the underlying form وَدَاد is Arabic.
Vedat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Vedat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Widād is not a Quranic personal name.
